Treasury yields hit multi-year highs Monday — the 10-year touched a fresh 19-year peak near 5.27% and the 30-year jumped to 5.55% — as traders brace for the Fed to keep tightening into elevated inflation.
Major indices fell Monday with over 65% of S&P 500 issues lower; only Health Care, Staples and Energy sectors advanced while Financials, Industrials and Communication Services led declines.
Gold sold off sharply (roughly -3% to -4%) on rate-hike bets while Bitcoin also declined, and the VIX rose nearly 10% as risk appetite cooled.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.news: Nvidia launched its Open Agent Safety Platform on Sept. 28, combining software guardrails (OpenShell) and hardware-level monitoring (Sentry via BlueField-4 DPUs) to contain autonomous AI agents. More than 100 organizations including Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, Palantir, CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks are working with the platform, and Nvidia said it could have prevented a July containment breach involving AI agents.
items.risk: Premarket reaction was mixed (some reports show a modest dip) and shares are already up sharply for the year, leaving room for profit-taking on a 'sell the news' reaction.
items.entry: Dip to $226.27–228.08, or break above $233.21 on volume

items.name: Carnival Corporation & plc
items.news: Carnival reports fiscal Q3 2026 results before today's open, with consensus near $1.35-$1.36 EPS on about $8.4B revenue. The cruise operator has beaten Zacks estimates in each of its last four quarters (average surprise of ~18%) and carries a Street 'Strong Buy' consensus from 20 of 27 covering analysts.
items.risk: Analysts have been trimming EPS estimates recently on the crude-oil rally raising fuel costs, so a soft Q4 guide or fuel-cost commentary could trigger a sharp post-earnings swing in either direction.
items.entry: Dip to $21.77–22.03, or break above $23.35 on volume

items.name: Liberty Energy Inc
items.news: Barclays upgraded Liberty Energy to Overweight from Equal-Weight on Sept. 28 with a $27 price target, joining a recent wave of upgrades from Goldman Sachs, BofA, Morgan Stanley, UBS, Stifel and RBC pointing to a completions-cycle inflection and growth in its Power business. The move comes as oil prices stay elevated on the Iran/Strait of Hormuz standoff.
items.risk: Oilfield-services stocks remain highly levered to crude prices and any Iran de-escalation or oil pullback could quickly unwind the current sentiment tailwind.
items.entry: Dip to $18.45–18.80, or break above $19.80 on volume

items.name: Royal Caribbean Group
items.news: Bank of America upgraded Royal Caribbean to Buy from Neutral on Sept. 28 with a $330 price target, a sector-positive call that lands the same week cruise-peer Carnival reports earnings.
items.risk: Cruise operators share exposure to rising fuel costs from the current oil rally, which could pressure margins across the group.
items.entry: Dip to $237.55–241.08, or break above $261.66 on volume

items.name: First Solar Inc
items.news: KeyBanc upgraded First Solar to Sector Weight from Underweight on Sept. 28, marking an improved sentiment shift for the solar-module maker.
items.risk: The upgrade is to a neutral 'Sector Weight,' not Overweight, and solar equities remain sensitive to interest-rate direction and policy headlines.
items.entry: Dip to $167.62–171.37, or break above $202.46 on volume

items.name: Snowflake Inc
items.news: Phillip Securities initiated Snowflake with a Buy rating and $423 price target on Sept. 28, adding a fresh bullish voice in enterprise software.
items.risk: New coverage initiations carry less market-moving weight than established-analyst upgrades, and high-multiple software names are vulnerable to the current rise in yields.
items.entry: Dip to $321.15–326.03, or break above $348.61 on volume

items.name: Nordic American Tankers Ltd
items.news: Crude tanker stocks including Nordic American Tankers, Frontline and DHT Holdings have surged this year as the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption force longer voyage routes, tightening effective vessel supply and lifting charter rates; shipping names have been hitting multi-year highs as the disruption persists.
items.risk: Tanker rates are highly cyclical and geopolitical premiums can fade quickly if Hormuz tensions ease or a ceasefire/sanctions deal advances.
items.entry: Dip to $7.63–7.74, or break above $7.98 on volume
